title: Measuring CPT-1-mediated respiration in permeabilized cells and isolated mitochondria
author: Yang, Doan, et al.

steps.title: Hydrate Seahorse XF cartridge
steps.instruction: Soak each well of the Seahorse XF cartridge in 200 µL of the manufacturer‑supplied XF calibrant, incubate at 37 °C in a humidified non‑CO₂ incubator for 8–48 h (typically overnight). This preparation takes 5–10 min on the day before the assay.

steps.title: Plate cells for permeabilized assay
steps.instruction: Two days before the assay, harvest HepG2 cells (ATCC HB‑8065) and resuspend at 2.5 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹. Plate 100 µL (2.5 × 10⁴ cells) into each of the inner 60 wells of a Seahorse XF96 plate using a multichannel pipette; keep the cell suspension well‑mixed by pipetting up and down before each dispense. Fill the outer wells with 200 µL PBS or culture medium to minimize edge effects.

steps.title: Treat plate with Cell‑Tak (if needed)
steps.instruction: For non‑adherent cells, coat the assay plate with Cell‑Tak according to the manufacturer’s instructions, then wash and dry the plate. This coating step requires 1 h on the day of the experiment.

steps.title: Pre‑chill equipment for mitochondria isolation
steps.instruction: Set all centrifuges to 4 °C. Pre‑chill homogenizers, glassware, plasticware, buffers (MSHE + BSA), and tubes on ice, and keep everything cold throughout the isolation.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse and collect liver
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse with isoflurane followed by cervical dislocation (IACUC‑approved). Spray the carcass with ethanol, make a U‑shaped incision in the lower abdomen, and quickly excise the liver with forceps/scissors. Place the liver into a 50 mL beaker containing just enough ice‑cold MSHE + BSA to cover the tissue.

steps.title: Mince liver and replace buffer
steps.instruction: While the beaker remains on ice, mince the liver with scissors. Frequently allow tissue to settle, then pour off the cloudy medium containing blood, fat, and connective tissue. Add fresh MSHE + BSA and repeat mincing and draining until the tissue is finely minced and the buffer is clear.

steps.title: Homogenize liver tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the minced liver to a pre‑chilled 15 mL Teflon glass homogenizer receptacle, adding MSHE + BSA to fill roughly three‑quarters of the narrow part of the tube. Homogenize with a drill‑driven Teflon pestle for 2–3 strokes until the mixture is homogeneous and free of debris.

steps.title: First centrifugation (low speed)
steps.instruction: Divide the homogenate into two pre‑chilled centrifuge tubes and bring each to ~four‑fifths of the tube volume with MSHE + BSA. Centrifuge at 1 000 g for 3 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Filter supernatant through cheesecloth
steps.instruction: While the tubes spin, wet two layers of muslin or cheesecloth with MSHE + BSA and place them over the mouth of a clean, pre‑chilled conical tube. Decant the supernatant through the wet cloth into two new pre‑chilled tubes, taking care not to spill. If cheesecloth is unavailable, use a 70 µm cell strainer.

steps.title: Second centrifugation (mitochondrial pellet)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered supernatant at 11 600 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash mitochondrial pellet
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, resuspend each pellet in 50–100 µL MSHE + BSA, combine the two resuspensions into a single tube, and centrifuge again at 11 600 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final resuspension of mitochondria
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, carefully remove as much of the light, ‘fluffy’ edge of the dark brown pellet as possible, and resuspend the remaining pellet in 20–100 µL MSHE **without** BSA (keep on ice). Do not add BSA at this stage because it interferes with protein quantification. The concentrated mitochondria remain viable for several hours on ice.

steps.title: Determine mitochondrial protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein content of the mitochondrial suspension using a standard assay (e.g., Bradford or BCA). From an 8–10‑week‑old mouse liver, expect 15–30 mg total mitochondrial protein.

steps.title: Analyze respiration data (post‑run)
steps.instruction: For each well, calculate: (1) Maximal FCCP‑stimulated respiration = MAX(FCCP) – Rot/AA; (2) Phosphorylating respiration = ADP – Oligo.; (3) Proton leak = Oligo. – Rot/AA. Use the average of the two baseline measurements before each injection, except for FCCP where the single highest value is used. Adjust all values for background respiration insensitive to rotenone and antimycin A.

description: This protocol is written for use with a Seahorse XF Analyzer, but the approach is broadly adaptable to other plate-based fluorescent or platinum electrode-based techniques to measure oxygen consumption. A full list of critical reagents and consumables is provided in the key resources table. Each section will be split when appropriate to provide specific information for use of this protocol with permeabilized cells or isolated mitochondria. Cultured hepatocytes and isolated liver mitochondria are used as examples, but this analysis can be extended to any cell or tissue type with suitable rates of oxidation for the substrate(s) of interest (e.g., long-chain fatty acids). We present both protocols to provide as broad of a resource as possible: when starting with cultured cells it is almost always preferable to work with permeabilized cells over isolated mitochondria, whereas working with animal tissue often lends itself to isolating mitochondria. This protocol was used previously to determine the on-target concentration of the CPT-1 inhibitor etomoxir and its off-target effects on oxidative phosphorylation (Divakaruni et al., 2018). Prior to using this protocol, researchers should familiarize themselves with a standardized, intact cell respirometry assay with the Seahorse XF Analyzer (Gotoh et al., 2021; Gu et al., 2021; Pelletier et al., 2014). All Seahorse XF experiments require the measurement cartridge to be hydrated in proprietary calibrant for 8–48 h (usually overnight) prior to the assay. Hydrate the Seahorse XF cartridge (from the Extracellular Flux Assay Kit) by soaking fluorophores in 200 μL of manufacturer-supplied XF calibrant per well according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The cartridge should be incubated at 37°C in a humidified, non-CO2 incubator overnight (i.e., 8–20 h). This step takes 5–10 min on the day prior to the assay.
